text.p: Texaco Inc stock is volatile and can expected to remain so while its civil rights problems are in the news, Dean Witter analyst Eugene L. Nowak said.
The stock closed off 1-1/8 at 100-7/8 in heavy trading on Tuesday after climbing as high as 102-1/2 in the market's early rally and dropping to 98-7/8 on the ensuing selloff.
"It's a volatile stock, especially with Jesse Jackson" continuing to seek boycotts of its products, Nowak said.
Jackson's coalition said Tuesday it would continue to boycott Texaco until it produces a plan to implement the civil rights commitment in its bias suit settlement.

Nowak said Tuesday's trading of nearly 1.3 million shares was "not an inordinate volume for this stock," and noted trading topped two million shares serveral days during the initial civil rights turmoil.
Others said Tuesday's volume could be the result of selling by state pension funds, although Nowak sees more threats than action from these institutions.
The "only way (the boycott) could hurt (Texaco) is by damaging the deal with Shell," said Carl H. Pforzheimer & Co analyst Albert J. Anton Jr.
The Royal Dutch/Shell Group subsidiary and Texaco are discussing a joint refining and marketing operation in the United States.
So far such talk is "just rumors," he said, adding the situation does "open pandora's box for Shell" Oil Co.
